It's mainly just ease of use and aesthetics, there are no huge differences. First it's easier to type apt versus apt-get, second it uses the color output in the terminal and third it uses a progress bar for installs where apt-get doesn't.

This explains the difference in more detail.

https://debian-handbook.info/browse/stable/sect.apt-get.html

Plus -get install is redundant.

Let's get rid of both and store this in /usr/local/bin/apt

#!/usr/bin/env node
var spawn = require('child_process').spawn;
var commands = {update:1,upgrade:1,install:1,remove:1,autoremove:1,purge:1,source:1,'build-dep':1,'dist-upgrade':1,'dselect-upgrade':1,clean:1,autoclean:1,check:1,changelog:1,download:1};
var arglist=process.argv.slice(2);
if(!commands[arglist[0]]) {
 arglist=['install'].concat(arglist); 
}
spawn('apt-get',arglist,{stdio:[process.stdin,process.stdout,process.stderr]});
